# rallicagram

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview

`rallicagram` is a R wrapper for the [Gallicagram](https://www.gallicagram.com/) API. 

[Gallicagram](https://www.gallicagram.com/) is a super nice tool and set of databases that enables to easily run simple Natural Language Processing (**NLP**) analyses on a wide set of corpora. In particular, it enables to build historical **time series of occurrences of keywords** in various media in one line of code.

## Installation

You can install the development version of rallicagram from [GitHub](https://github.com/vincentbagilet/rallicagram) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("vincentbagilet/rallicagram")
```

## Usage

The main function, `gallicagram`, builds a data frame with the yearly, monthly or daily proportion of mentions of a term.

```{r usage}
library(rallicagram)

gallicagram(keyword = "président", corpus = "lemonde", from = 1960)
```

It enables to draw nice graphs representing the evolution of the use of a term in time, in two lines of code.

```{r graph, dpi=300, out.width="70%", fig.align = "center", echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(mediocrethemes)
set_mediocre_all(theme = theme_idid)

gallicagram(keyword = "obama", from = 2005) |> 
  gallicagraph()
```

The package also allows to describe co-occurrences or words associated with a keyword. The corresponding functions are described in the [vignette](articles/rallicagram.html).

## Corpora

The corpora available via Gallicagram are the following. Note, for now, there are two "Le Monde" corpora, with different functions associated with each (this is a feature of the data base and will evolve shortly).

```{r list_corpora, echo=FALSE}
rallicagram::list_corpora |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    number_of_words = ifelse(is.na(nb_words), "-", nb_words),
    available_functions = ifelse(is.na(available_func), "-", available_func)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::select(
    corpus_name, dplyr::everything(), -alt_base, -nb_words, -available_func
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename_with(\(x) stringr::str_replace_all(x, "_", " ") |>  
                       stringr::str_to_title()) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

Additional information on Gallicagram can be found on a [preprint](https://osf.io/preprints/socarxiv/84bf3/) by Gallicagram developers [
Benoît de Courson](https://regicid.github.io/) and Benjamin Azoulay and on the "Notice" tab of the [Gallicagram website](https://www.gallicagram.com/).
